"We are confident about our supply through September." In an interview with Eneos' CFO Soichiro Tanaha on Thursday, he said that the situation has?become?much more stable.

events.content_detail:
# Iran begins talks with Japanese firms on oil sales under temporary US sanctions waiver

## A senior Iranian official said any deal would require the US to extend the current waiver given the shipping time between Japan and Iran.

[Follow us on **Google**](https://www.google.com/preferences/source?q=https://www.jpost.com/)

Iranian flag with stock graph and an oil pump jack miniature model are seen in this illustration taken October 9, 2023.

(photo credit: REUTERS/DADO RUVIC/ILLUSTRATION/FILE PHOTO)

ByREUTERS

Iran has begun talks with Japanese companies under a [US sanctions waiver](https://www.jpost.com/middle-east/iran-news/article-899961) allowing it to resume oil sales, though prospective buyers are seeking a longer waiver and reassurances about ship safety, three Iranian and Western sources said.

The waiver, part of 60-day peace talks between Tehran and Washington, was issued on June 22 and expires August 21.

Three Japanese buyers were looking at possible crude oil purchases from Iran, their first since 2019, said two Iranian sources, who declined to be identified due to the sensitivity of the issue.

Japanese and [Iranian officials](https://www.jpost.com/international/article-901291) were in initial talks about possible oil sales, a Western industry source familiar with the matter said separately.

An official at Japan's Ministry of Economy, Trade and Industry (METI), which oversees fuel supply infrastructure, said he was unaware of any such matter.

# Iran, Oman reached agreement on Strait of Hormuz based on US MoU, Parliament Speaker Ghalibaf says

## "The Israelis are undoubtedly seeking to disrupt the Iran-US MoU," Ghalibaf added, "but the deterrent power of the Islamic Republic of Iran in the region will prevent them from starting a war again."

[Follow us on **Google**](https://www.google.com/preferences/source?q=https://www.jpost.com/)

Iranian parliament speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf (L) shakes hands with Omani Foreign Minister Badr bin Hamad Al Busaidi (R) before a meeting in Muscat, Oman, on June 22, 2026.

(photo credit: Hamed Malekpour / Middle East Images / AFP via Getty Images)

By[TZVI JASPER](/author/tzvi-jasper)

Iran and Oman have come to an agreement regarding the regulation of traffic in the Strait of Hormuz, based on Article V of the Memorandum of Understanding with the United States, Iranian Parliament Speaker [Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf](https://www.jpost.com/international/article-901291) announced during a meeting with Chinese officials on Friday.

"The Israelis are undoubtedly seeking to disrupt the Iran-US [Memorandum of Understanding](https://www.jpost.com/tags/memorandum-of-understanding)," Ghalibaf added, "but the deterrent power of the Islamic Republic of Iran in the region will prevent them from starting a war again."

Ghalibaf also resolved that the United States would not be allowed to interfere in the management of the [Strait of Hormuz](https://www.jpost.com/middle-east/article-901050).

# Chinese excavator tariff ‘inconsistent with net zero’

03 Jul 2026 By [Ian Weinfass](https://www.constructionnews.co.uk/author/ian-weinfass/ "Posts by Ian Weinfass")

![Legal_shutterstock_140867215.webp](https://cdn.ca.emap.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/8/2026/03/Legal_shutterstock_140867215.webp)

A lawyer acting for Chinese equipment manufacturer LiuGong Machinery UK has said UK import tariffs on certain electric excavators are “inconsistent” with the government’s net-zero ambitions.

Anti-dumping duties ranging from 18.81 per cent to 40.08 per cent have applied to certain excavators imported from China since May 2025, following a Trade Remedies Authority (TRA) investigation into allegations that they were being dumped on the UK market.

In 2025, the TRA reconsidered aspects of its decision [after LiuGong Group and Caterpillar challenged it](https://www.constructionnews.co.uk/supply-chain/tra-reconsiders-tariffs-on-chinese-excavator-imports-14-07-20
